## The 8-axis conflict map (performance + production controls)

- **Erotic pull:** E Dorian-blues stability; sus/add11 warmth; “home” feels seductive and safe.

### Axis 2 — **Rhythmic grid (inverted tribal pocket as temptation)**
- **Erotic pull:** upright bass/upbeat counter-melody feels like pursuit (hips/heartbeat) without saying anything explicit.

### Axis 3 — **Vocal register & proximity (mic = intimacy vs distance = judgment)**
- **Erotic pull:** close-mic low tenor, breath present, consonants softened, slight vocal fry.

```

# 2) `song-excellence.yaml` (Quality + Creative Scoring Layer)
```yaml
rubric_version: 1.0.0
rubric:
  dimensions:
    - id: theme_clarity
      weight: 0.12
      description: "Theme is legible to a listener without extra explanation."
      pass_threshold: 0.70
    - id: emotional_arc
      weight: 0.15
      description: "Tension/release, escalation, and payoff feel earned."
    - id: conflict_execution
      weight: 0.15
      description: "The erotic/spiritual conflict is audible in performance/arrangement."
    - id: originality
      weight: 0.10
      description: "Fresh phrasing/sonics; not generic genre pastiche."
    - id: vocal_authority
      weight: 0.12
      description: "Lead sounds believable; choir functions as character."
    - id: groove_integrity
      weight: 0.10
      description: "Pocket is intentional; syncopation supports story."
    - id: arrangement_readability
      weight: 0.10
      description: "Sections are distinct; listener can follow."
    - id: mix_translation
      weight: 0.08
      description: "Core elements translate across speakers; mono-center discipline."
    - id: audience_resonance
      weight: 0.08
      description: "Likely to connect beyond niche; hook and emotional access."
  output:
    scoring_scale: [0.0, 1.0]
    overall_pass: 0.78
    return:
      - overall_score
      - dimension_scores
      - top_3_strengths
      - top_3_risks
      - recommended_actions
guardrails:
  content:
    keep_sexual_content: "suggestive_not_explicit"
    consent_language: "affirmative_agency_preferred"
```

# 3) `template-creative-ust.yaml` (Output Canon / Human-First Spec)
```yaml
project:
  id: "crave-remix-001"
  title: "Crave (Conflict Remix)"
  version: "0.1.0"
deliverable:
  type: remix
  goal: "Make the conflict itself the performance deliverable (flesh vs spirit), no lyric rewrites; adlibs + arrangement convey baptism/struggle."
lyrics:
  locked: true
  edits_allowed: [adlibs, arrangement_only]
style:
  genre: "Southern Americana × Gospel Blues Fusion"
  mood: [heated, reverent, conflicted, resilient]
audio:
  tempo_bpm: 128
  key_center: "E minor"
  mode_palette:
    - "Dorian-Blues hybrid"
    - "Phrygian dominant borrowing (tension spikes)"
arrangement:
  roadmap: [Intro, Verse1, PreChorus, Chorus, Verse2, Bridge, Chorus2, Outro]
  conflict_plan:
    characters:
      flesh_voice: {mic: "close", reverb: "short plate", pitch: "blue curls allowed"}
      spirit_voice: {mic: "distant/room", fx: "preacher echo", pitch: "straighter, authoritative"}
    section_notes:
      Intro: "Consent/intimacy framed; spirit enters as distant warning"
      PreChorus: "guilt spike via harmonic borrow + choir response"
      Bridge: "exorcism/altar-call energy; strip-down; B minor turn"
performance:
  vocals:
    lead:
      profile: "male low tenor, smoky drawl -> gospel belt"
      gestures: [whisper_doubles, preacher_cadence, yell_ins]
    choir:
      role: "conscience/Spirit character, not decoration"
      stacks: "3-part, distant room"
adlibs:
  bank:
    flesh_close: ["mm-hmm", "can't lie", "I crave it"]
    spirit_distant: ["Lord have mercy", "hold on", "wash me", "amen", "make me clean"]
  placement_rules:
    - "Overlap flesh+spirit adlibs on chorus peak for collision"
    - "Reserve 'wash me/make me clean' for bridge->final chorus"
sound:
  instruments:
    organ: "moral authority"
    lap_steel: "skin/touch memory"
    upright_bass: "upbeat pursuit engine"
  fx_palette: [tape_hiss, floorboard_creak, thunder_crack, room_bleed]
mix:
  priorities:
    - "Lead + upright bass mono-center"
    - "Choir wide, distant"
    - "Keep 35-70Hz controlled (upright + tom)"
ip:
  notes:
    - "Remix: arrangement/adlibs only; preserve original lyric authorship splits"
change_log:
  - v: "0.1.0"
    change: "Initial conflict blueprint spec"
```

  \ Song Excellence Matrix (compact rubric) Scale: 0–5 (0 = missing; 1 = very weak; 2 = weak; 3 = competent; 4 = strong; 5\
  \ = outstanding) Weight = relative importance. Multiply score × weight. Max possible weighted sum = 100. # Criterion (what\
  \ to evaluate) Weight (%) Minimum pass (score) Notes / Measurement 1 Hook Strength (melodic + lyrical memorability) 18 4\
  \ Hook=chorus/lead motif; earworm test (hum after 30s) 2 Lyric Integrity & Emotional Clarity 12 3 Narrative coherence; truthfulness;\
  \ no lyric edits outside [Lyric Block] 3 Vocal Delivery & Character 10 3 Tone, timing, persona fit, intelligibility 4 Melody\
  \ & Topline Craft 10 3 Contour, singability, interval choices 5 Structure & Pacing (arrangement) 8 3 Section balance; hook\
  \ placement; dynamics arc 6 Production Quality (mix basics) 12 3 Balance, low-end clarity, vocal sit, no clipping 7 Arrangement\
  \ Interest & Contrast 6 2 Transitions, automation, instrumentation choices 8 Commercial Viability & Market Fit 8 3 Tempo/genre\
  \ fit, DSP playlist targets, length 9 Originality / Distinctive Element 6 2 Unique twist, persona, sample, or production\
  \ idea 10 Metadata & Governance (tags, credits, UST fields) 4 3 Semicolons, persona_map, CREW_TAGS, release metadata completeness\
  \ 11 Lyric Syllable Integrity (Suno rule 6–10) 4 4 All lines in [Lyric Block] between 6–10 syllables 12 Pre-release QA Checks\
  \ (deliverables) 2 2 WAV/LUFS/ISRC, stems, stems naming, integration ledger entry Scoring example: If a track gets scores\
  \ S1..S12, composite = Σ(Si × weight_i). Pass threshold = 70/100 (recommendation). If composite is 60–69, require 1 targeted\
  \ revision pass. <70 = iterate. Quick scoring guide (how to rate consistently) 5 (Outstanding): Distinct, repeatable evidence;\
  \ passes creative & technical checks; audience reaction likely. 4 (Strong): Clear commercial promise; minor polish needed.\
  \ 3 (Competent): Works; needs non-trivial polish. 2 (Weak): Noticeable problems; rework required. 1 (Very weak): Core elements\
  \ missing or incompatible with release. 0 (Missing): Criterion absent. For binary checks (e.g., metadata present) use 0\
  \ or 5 only, then convert to scale. Decision Tree — Go / No-Go / Iterate (compact) Metadata Gate — Are required metadata\
  \ fields present and valid? (Y → 2; N → HOLD: fix metadata) Lyric Syllable Gate — Do all lines in [Lyric Block] meet 6–10\
  \ syllables? (Y → 3; N → ITERATE: edit phrasing or overlay fills, not lyric rewrite if integrity lock applies) Hook Gate\
  \ — Hook Strength ≥ 4? (Y → 4; N → ITERATE: rewrite topline/hook) Composite Score — Composite ≥ 70? (Y → RELEASE candidate;\
  \ 60–69 → TARGETED REVISION; <60 → MAJOR REWORK) Production Gate — Mix check pass (LUFS, no clipping, low-end clarity)?\
  \ (Y → Release prep; N → Mix pass & re-evaluate) Final QA — Stems exported; Integration ledger updated; release pack ready?\
  \ (Y → PUSH TO DISTRIBUTION; N → Finish deliverables) Use this tree for rapid audit before sending to mastering/distribution.\n\

  \ and gating as well as creative thinking... what do those terms mean to each and what published artifacts have they shared\n\
  002 | In short: Quality control in music means the systematic checks producers use to ensure a track is technically polished\
  \ and emotionally consistent before release. Gating refers to decision points (or “release gates”) where a song either passes,\
  \ requires revision, or is held back. Creative thinking is the exploratory, imaginative process producers and writers use\
  \ to generate originality and emotional resonance. Each genre’s hitmakers interpret these terms differently, and many have\
  \ shared artifacts—interviews, essays, production notes, or scholarly studies—that illustrate their approach.\n```\n\n##\
  \ S0287\n\n```text\n001 | \U0001F3A4 Pop Producers (Max Martin, Jack Antonoff)\n002 | Quality Control: Pop hitmakers emphasize\
  \ hook clarity, mix precision, and playlist readiness. QC is about ensuring songs meet radio/DSP standards.\n```\n\n## S0288\n\
  \n```text\n001 | Gating: They use “chorus tests” (can you hum it after 30 seconds?) as a go/no-go gate.\n```\n\n## S0289\n\
  \n```text\n001 | Creative Thinking: Balancing formula with surprise—Antonoff often discusses “emotional honesty” in liner\
  \ notes and interviews.\n```\n\n## S0290\n\n```text\n001 | Artifacts: Max Martin’s interviews in Billboard and Antonoff’s\
  \ essays in Rolling Stone highlight their QC and creative processes.\n```\n\n## S0291\n\n```text\n001 | \U0001F920 Country\
  \ Producers (Dan Huff, Joey Moi)\n002 | Quality Control: Focus on storytelling integrity and vocal authenticity. QC ensures\
  \ lyrics feel true to lived experience.\n```\n\n## S0292\n\n```text\n001 | Gating: Nashville often uses “radio room” listening\
  \ sessions as gates—if programmers don’t bite, the song iterates.\n```\n\n## S0293\n\n```text\n001 | Creative Thinking:\
  \ Blending tradition with modern polish. Huff has spoken about “keeping the steel guitar alive” in interviews.\n```\n\n\
  ## S0294\n\n```text\n001 | Artifacts: Published credits and liner notes in Nashville trade journals; ASCAP interviews on\
  \ songwriting craft.\n```\n\n## S0295\n\n```text\n001 | \U0001F3B6 Soul / R&B Producers (Hitmaka, No I.D.)\n002 | Quality\
  \ Control: QC is about emotional resonance and mix warmth. No I.D. stresses “truth in sound.”\n```\n\n## S0296\n\n```text\n\
  001 | Gating: Audience vibe checks—if the track doesn’t move listeners in studio previews, it’s gated.\n```\n\n## S0297\n\
  \n```text\n001 | Creative Thinking: Improvisation and layering; Hitmaka describes “building vibe before lyrics” in interviews.\n\

  ```\n\n## S0299\n\n```text\n001 | \U0001F33E Americana / Acoustic Rock Producers (Dave Cobb, T Bone Burnett)\n002 | Quality\
  \ Control: QC means authenticity—no overproduction. Cobb insists on live takes as QC.\n```\n\n## S0300\n\n```text\n001 |\
  \ Gating: Songs are gated by “emotional truth”—if the artist can’t deliver it live, it’s held back.\n```\n\n## S0301\n\n\

  ```text\n001 | ## 0) System Identity\n002 | This workspace defines a **portable, zero-touch, end-to-end prompt architecture**\
  \ for converting human song intent into **Suno-ready output** using a **Technical UST** and strict formatting governance.\
  \ All dialogue is treated as **development worklogs**. All corrections are **Change Requests (CRs)** that update canon via\
  \ versioned lineage.\n```\n\n## S2018\n\n```text\n001 | Core objectives:\n002 | - Raise the bar of **song excellence** using\
  \ auditability, gating, and measurable KPIs.\n003 | - Validate that the **UST prototype is Suno-efficient** by matching\
  \ how Suno interprets and expands the UST.\n004 | - Produce **monolithic, modular, end-to-end prompts** that a brand-new\
  \ session can run without hidden context.\n```\n\n## S2019\n\n```text\n001 | ---\n```\n\n## S2020\n\n```text\n001 | ## 1)\
  \ Canonical Output Artifacts\n002 | ### A) Technical UST (Suno-facing)\n003 | A structured session container composed of\
  \ meta-containers and fields:\n004 | - `[Theory]` mode, tonal center, meter, tempo, chord color\n005 | - `[Voice]` register,\
  \ delivery, expression, articulation\n006 | - `[Style]` genre, era, intent, texture, aesthetic, focus\n007 | - `[Timbre]`\
  \ drum tone, bass tone, keyboard tone, guitar tone, fx palette, vocal tone\n008 | - `[Performance]` execution, gesture,\
  \ rhythm handling, touch, phrasing ops\n009 | - `[Post]` comp, eq, space, dynamics, mastering targets, mix notes\n010 |\
  \ - `[Operators]` optional transformations and directives\n011 | - `[Validators]` enforcement rules (punctuation, attribution,\
  \ lint)\n```\n\n## S2021\n\n```text\n001 | ### B) Lyrics Block (Tactical + Atomic)\n002 | A sequence of section blocks that\
  \ must remain Suno-compatible:\n003 | - Section header line (succinct directive form)\n004 | - Optional `[ ** sFX: ... **\
  \ ]` stage-direction blocks (non-vocal)\n005 | - Quoted lyric lines `\"...\"` only\n006 | - Optional parenthetical adlibs\
  \ `(\"...\")` after lyric lines\n```\n\n## S2022\n\n```text\n001 | ### C) Show Summary (Suno-facing)\n002 | A short professional\
  \ narrative describing the record as if briefing a producer/engineer.\n003 | Strict character discipline is required (target\
  \ short, avoid token waste, avoid comma issues).\n```\n\n## S2023\n\n```text\n001 | ### D) Governance Outputs (Quality +\
  \ Traceability)\n002 | - Validators pass/fail\n003 | - Excellence scoring (SEG) and decisions (G-Card)\n004 | - Chain report\
  \ (Q→A→F / CR lineage) where required\n```\n\n## S2024\n\n```text\n001 | ---\n```\n\n## S2025\n\n```text\n001 | ## 2) Suno\
  \ Translation Model (Observed Behavior)\n002 | Suno tends to:\n003 | - **Expand** UST shorthand into narrative prose per\
  \ container (Theory, Voice, Style, etc.).\n004 | - Respect **validators** when phrased as enforceable rules.\n005 | - Trigger\
  \ **content moderation/blocked words** on certain genre terms (example observed: “skank” blocked), requiring safe synonyming.\n\
  006 | - Treat commas as parsing friction, motivating a punctuation policy that quarantines commas inside quoted lyric text.\n\

  \ | ## 4) Formatting Canon for Suno Efficiency (Highest Priority)\n002 | ### 4.1 Section Header Standard (Must Use)\n003\
  \ | Section headers must be **succinct** and avoid schema-like tag clouds.\n```\n\n## S2032\n\n```text\n001 | **DO**\n002\
  \ | `[Worship Hook | 16 bars | Lead+BGV1 | worship call-and-response WITH stop-time entry AND full choir AND sax counterpoint\
  \ AND peak energy]`\n```\n\n## S2033\n\n```text\n001 | **DON’T**\n002 | `[Worship Hook | durationbars: 16 | who: Lead+BGV1\
  \ | mode: ... | feel/tags: ...]`\n```\n\n## S2034\n\n```text\n001 | Rules:\n002 | - Replace `durationbars: N` with `N bars`\
  \ (or `{x} bars`).\n003 | - No key/subkey labels in headers (`who:`, `mode:`, `tags:` etc.).\n004 | - Header must contain\
  \ only **variables and a directive sentence**, not field labels.\n```\n\n## S2035\n\n```text\n001 | ### 4.2 Stage Directions\
  \ Must Not Be Quoted\n002 | Stage direction examples belong in **sFX blocks**, not in quoted lyric lines.\n```\n\n## S2036\n\
  \n```text\n001 | **DO**\n002 | `[ ** sFX: Organ swells AND deepening bass WITH light hi-hats as the choir takes the lead.\
  \ ** ]`\n```\n\n## S2037\n\n```text\n001 | **DON’T**\n002 | `\"*(Organ swells, deepening bass, light hi-hats as the choir\
  \ takes the lead.)*\"`\n```\n\n## S2038\n\n```text\n001 | ### 4.3 First Lyric Line Placement\n002 | The first lyric line\
  \ must appear **exactly one line below the section header(s)**.\n003 | If present, sFX blocks appear between header and\
  \ the first quoted lyric line.\n```\n\n## S2039\n\n```text\n001 | ### 4.4 Speaker Attribution Canon (Critical)\n002 | Speaker\
  \ attribution uses **square-bracket performer tokens** only.\n003 | Colon labels are banned.\n```\n\n## S2040\n\n```text\n\
  001 | **DO**\n002 | `[Lead] \"Some say it’s like fire shut up in my bones…\"`\n```\n\n## S2041\n\n```text\n001 | **DON’T**\n\
  002 | `\"[Lead:] Some say it’s like fire shut up in my bones…\"`\n```\n\n## S2042\n\n```text\n001 | #### Choir and BGV Handling\

## 1) You solved the hardest fusion problem: one shared core
Your STYLE prompt doesn’t list genres like a playlist. It declares a **single sonic thesis**:

- **Tape-recorded acoustic session** (truth; air; human timing)  
- **Gospel roots** (moral language; ritual; call-and-response)  
- **Acoustic blues / Americana grit** (physical desire; dirt-under-nails tone; micro-bends)  
- **Tribal rhythms** (body; pulse; repetition; trance)

That’s why it feels unified instead of “stacked.” The shared core is **human voice in a real room over an honest pocket**. Everything else becomes flavor, not competition.

## 2) The sliders created the “sweet spot” between control and emergence
**Weirdness 68%**  
High enough to let the model *invent* connective tissue (unexpected voicings; phrasing quirks; microtonal bends; syncopation interpretation) without breaking coherence.

**Style Influence 67%**  
Keeps the output anchored to your declared identity: Southern Americana × gospel blues with tribal undercurrent. It prevents the engine from “generic pop/EDM”-ing a 128 BPM track.

**Audio Influence 67%**  
This is the “fidelity anchor.” It tends to preserve the *feel of an acoustic capture* (brush transients; upright detail; room tone) rather than letting the mix turn synthetic or overly glossy.

Net effect: **tight pocket + organic dirt + tasteful surprise**.

## 3) The Theory block is doing emotional storytelling, not just music theory
You picked a harmonic language that *already contains conflict*.

### Dorian-blues hybrid (home base)
- Dorian carries a **hopeful ache** (minor with a lifted color)
- Blues vocabulary carries **physical truth** (bends; grit; unresolved emotion)

So the default emotional state is “temptation that still has conscience.”

### Quarter-tone blue curls (bodily “tell”)
You didn’t just say “bluesy.” You specified **quarter-tone curls**, which gives the model permission to make the vocal intonation itself feel like *yielding*.

### Brief Phrygian dominant borrowing (conscience spike)
This is key: you framed it as **brief** and **for tension**. That creates momentary “church alarm bells” without rekeying the whole record into exotic cosplay. It reads as: *a flash of fear; then back into the craving.*

That’s “advanced” because it’s **harmonic dramaturgy**: the harmony acts like a character.

## 4) Your conflict deliverable is encoded as staging: close-mic flesh vs distant spirit
This is the most important part of why it lands.

- **Flesh voice** is implied by: close mic; dry; front-and-center; whisper doubles; pocket-locked intimacy  
- **Spirit voice** is implied by: distant room choir stacks; organ authority; preacher echo throws; ritual adlibs (“wash me”; “amen”; “have mercy”)

Because you specify *space and proximity*, the conflict becomes audible even if the base lyric is simple. The listener hears two rooms at once:
- the “private room” (breath; heat; closeness)
- the “church room” (distance; judgment; grace; ritual)

That’s how you make the theme the performance.

## 5) Rhythm design: 128 BPM that still feels like a ritual, not a club loop
The “inverted tribal grid” solves a common issue: fast tempo can kill gravitas.

- Brushes on **1 and 3** = restraint; sobriety; “hands folded”
- Upright + floor tom pressure on **2 and 4 upbeats** = body pull; forward lean; temptation engine
- Tight syncopation = modern momentum without trap clichés

So you get **drive** without losing **weight**.

## 6) Timbre choices reinforce the moral narrative (instrument roles are symbolic)
This prompt is “advanced” because each instrument has a *role*:

- **Upright bass** = heartbeat; pursuit; physical insistence  
- **Floor tom** = ritual drum; body/earth  
- **Organ** = moral authority; church air; verdict  
- **Lap steel** = touch memory; heat shimmer; longing  
- **Rhodes/pads** = compassion glue (bridges flesh/spirit without choosing sides)

When the arrangement “thins” in Verse 2 and “drops to organ and floor tom” in the Bridge, you’re basically staging a **courtroom / altar-call** moment using sound.

## 7) The adlib plan turns a simple chorus into theology without rewriting lyrics
You respected the remix constraint (don’t rewrite the song) but still created the baptism-conflict narrative by adding a second text layer.

- explicit voice geometry (mono center lead; distant choir; automation on plate/room)

Suno-style engines reward prompts that behave like **session direction** more than prompts that read like essays.

## How the GPT should analyze audio (what Data Analysis can do)
When you upload audio, it can run Python analysis (typical libraries: librosa; numpy; scipy). Practical metrics it can generate:

- **Tempo estimate** (with confidence range)
- **Spectral tilt** (is it dark; bright; harsh)
- **Low-end integrity** (boom vs tight; bass/tom overlap)
- **Stereo width + mono correlation**
- **Dynamic range / crest factor** (is it crushed; too flat)
- **Section change detection** (approximate: novelty curve)

Then it maps those back to your prompt claims:
- “tight pocket” vs actual transient smearing
- “upright bass warm wood” vs sub-heavy mud
- “lead front-and-center” vs vocal buried
- “tape feel” vs sterile high-end

## FOIL 4-tier contract (sandbox spec v0.1)
You just defined the missing spine: a **4-tier cascade** that works like configuration inheritance, but with FOIL coverage and upward dedupe.

### Tier 1 — MACRO (globals)
**Purpose:** global identity; defaults; what applies everywhere unless overridden  
**Where it lives:** **STYLE PROMPT** is the canonical MACRO container  
**Examples:**
- overall genre blend  
- recording reality (tape; live room; acoustic session)  
- global instrumentation palette  
- global mixing intent (stereo discipline; mono low end)  
- global “language rules” (no commas outside lyric quotes; choir as adlibs; etc)

**Rule:** if it’s true 80–100% of the song, it belongs in MACRO

---

### Tier 2 — MICRO (axis values)
**Purpose:** stable “module settings” per axis; defines how the song behaves in general  
**Where it lives:** your UST meta containers: Theory; Voice; Style; Timbre; Performance; Post  
**Shape:** `macro.key.subkey.variable+1` starts here

- **macro** = the container family (Theory; Voice; Style; Timbre; Performance; Post)  
- **key** = the field group (Voice.register; Timbre.guitar tone; etc)  
- **subkey** = internal split (lead; doubles; choir; left/right; etc)  
- **variable** = the actual value string  
- **+1** = one extra control knob that attaches behavior to the value (priority; trigger; constraint; exception; “only on hook”; etc)

**Example (conceptual):**  
- `Voice.register.lead = male low tenor`  
- `Voice.register.lead +1 = mono_center_priority`  
- `Theory.mode = Dorian blues hybrid`  
- `Theory.mode +1 = microtonal_curl_on_trigger_words`

---

### Tier 3 — TACTICAL (section headers; roadmap; repeats)
**Purpose:** section-level staging; “what changes when”  
**Where it lives:** section header lines; sFX blocks; Road‑Map order; repeat directives  
**This maps to:** `stanza.section header`  
You’re stripping the fat from headers (good) but keeping the **minimum tactical skeleton** so Suno can still “feel” sectional contrast.

**Rule:** Tactical contains *structure* and *override calls*, not long descriptors.

---

### Tier 4 — VARIABLE+1 (atomic line and word controls)
**Purpose:** line-level and word-level “switches”  
**Where it lives:** lyric lines; adlibs; word triggers; per-line sFX macros; per-word emphasis  
**This maps to:** `line.word`

This is where you get:
- word-triggered FX (delay throw only on “not like them”)  
- word-triggered pitch behavior (quarter-tone curl on “Suno”; straight pitch elsewhere)  
- per-line performer tokens (Lead only unless true multi primary)  
- adlib placement without creating fake second speakers

---

## The FOIL “math” part: cascade + composition
FOIL becomes operational when you treat the 4 tiers as a **merge stack**:

**Effective instruction at render-time** =  
MACRO defaults  
⊕ MICRO axis settings  
⊕ TACTICAL section overrides  
⊕ VARIABLE+1 atomic triggers

Where ⊕ means “merge; later tiers override earlier ones only where specified”.

This is also what makes **duplicate term promotion** deterministic.

---

## Duplicate Promotion Up-Shift (how duplicates move upward)
This is your “shift duplicate terms upwards” rule rewritten in FOIL terms:

### Up-shift rules
1) If a word-trigger or adlib repeats across many lines inside one section → promote it to the **TACTICAL section header** as a rule  
2) If a tactical rule repeats across multiple sections → promote it to **MICRO** (axis-level)  
3) If a micro rule repeats across most songs in your identity → promote it to **MACRO** (style prompt global)

### Why it works
- It reduces token waste  
- It reduces contradictions  
- It makes your system easier to “compile” into Suno-friendly text

---

## Sheet music “REPEAT logic” (sandbox grammar v0.1)
You’re right: you should not retype the chorus four times like prose.

### Internal repeat primitives (for your system)
These are **not necessarily Suno-facing**. They’re **compiler-facing**.

- `RPT(section_id; xN)`  
- `TAG(lines; xN)`  
- `VAMP(section_id; until:fade)`  
- `ENDING(1|2; section_id)`  
- `DS_AL_CODA(from:section_id; to:section_id)` (optional advanced)

### Practical constraint
Suno often behaves best when the **final prompt contains explicit lyrics** for repeated sections.

So:  
- **Internal UST** can use repeat logic  
- **Serializer/Compiler pass** expands it into explicit repeated section blocks before render

That gives you both:
- token efficiency in authoring  
- reliability at render time

---

## Mapping your two notations together (the bridge you asked for)

### “macro.key.subkey.variable+1”
This is the schema shape.

### “stanza.section header.line.word”
This is the lyric surface shape.

**Mapping:**
- stanza ≈ Tactical grouping (Intro; Verse; Chorus; Bridge; Outro)  
- section header ≈ Tactical header line + sFX block  
- line ≈ Variable (quoted lyric line)  
- word ≈ Variable+1 trigger surface (a word can carry a +1 behavior)

---

## Concrete application to “nOT lIKE tHEM” (no lyric changes; just reframing)
Here’s how your chorus repetition becomes FOIL-clean without rewriting lyrics.

### MICRO (declare once)
- HookWord = `not like them`  
- TriggerWordFX:
  - `not like them` → preacher_delay_throw  
  - `Suno` → quarter_tone_curl  
  - `equal` → diminished_lead_tone_hint  
- GlobalGesture = `clap on three`  
- ChoirRole = `adlib_echo_only` unless MultiPrimary true

### TACTICAL Road‑Map (with repeats)
- Intro  
- Chorus_A

- Verse_2  
- Chorus_B (bigger lift)  
- Bridge

- Outro (phone band)

### VARIABLE+1 (word level)
Inside the chorus lines, you don’t rewrite anything. You attach behaviors:
- “our Suno not like them” +1 = delay_throw_on_them  
- “all AI ain’t equal” +1 = straight_pitch_on_equal_then_blue_curl_release  
- adlibs remain parenthetical echoes

## The big takeaway (sandbox)
You’re defining a **compiler-grade cascade**:
- STYLE prompt = global MACRO truth  
- UST axes = MICRO defaults  
- section headers = TACTICAL staging and override calls  
- lyric lines and word triggers = VARIABLE+1 atomic control surface

I had suspected that 'Suno' was based on a triad of intertwined inputs: and the order of their appearance onscreen carried weight in importance. The triad I hypothesized was based upon the collision of the three macro level prompts on the web interface (and our respective terminology):

Harry & The Juke Joints v5.5
Name this Voice
Harry & The Juke Joints v5.5
Styles (optional)
Add styles
Description (optional)
Harry and The Juke Joints represent convergence. This persona is less about individual expression and more about collective motion. It captures the energy of a crowded room where music is participatory rather than presentational. The Juke Joints sound is built on groove—rhythms designed to move bodies before minds catch up.  Instrumentation emphasizes live interplay. Drums breathe, basslines wander, guitars converse with keys. Modern production techniques are layered on top, not to sterilize but to amplify. Sub-bass reinforces kick patterns, spatial FX extend room ambience, and arrangement automation mirrors the ebb and flow of a live set.  Narratively, this persona shifts focus from introspection to shared experience. Lyrics are simpler, refrains repeat, and hooks are designed for memorability rather than subtlety. This is intentional. Harry and The Juke Joints are about release—music as temporary suspension of burden. The stories are still there, but they are carried by rhythm rather than exposition.  In the MoMoney Studios ecosystem, this collaboration functions as a social catalyst. It is deployed when projects require momentum, accessibility, or communal resonance. Harry and The Juke Joints remind the system that music’s oldest function was not branding or therapy, but gathering. Their role is to turn narrative weight into movement, ensuring that even the heaviest truths can still dance.".

  002 | In short: Quality control in music means the systematic checks producers use to ensure a track is technically polished\
  \ and emotionally consistent before release. Gating refers to decision points (or “release gates”) where a song either passes,\
  \ requires revision, or is held back. Creative thinking is the exploratory, imaginative process producers and writers use\
  \ to generate originality and emotional resonance. Each genre’s hitmakers interpret these terms differently, and many have\
  \ shared artifacts—interviews, essays, production notes, or scholarly studies—that illustrate their approach.\n```\n\n##\
  \ S0287\n\n```text\n001 | \U0001F3A4 Pop Producers (Max Martin, Jack Antonoff)\n002 | Quality Control: Pop hitmakers emphasize\
  \ hook clarity, mix precision, and playlist readiness. QC is about ensuring songs meet radio/DSP standards.\n```\n\n## S0288\n\
  \n```text\n001 | Gating: They use “chorus tests” (can you hum it after 30 seconds?) as a go/no-go gate.\n```\n\n## S0289\n\
  \n```text\n001 | Creative Thinking: Balancing formula with surprise—Antonoff often discusses “emotional honesty” in liner\
  \ notes and interviews.\n```\n\n## S0290\n\n```text\n001 | Artifacts: Max Martin’s interviews in Billboard and Antonoff’s\
  \ essays in Rolling Stone highlight their QC and creative processes.\n```\n\n## S0291\n\n```text\n001 | \U0001F920 Country\
  \ Producers (Dan Huff, Joey Moi)\n002 | Quality Control: Focus on storytelling integrity and vocal authenticity. QC ensures\
  \ lyrics feel true to lived experience.\n```\n\n## S0292\n\n```text\n001 | Gating: Nashville often uses “radio room” listening\
  \ sessions as gates—if programmers don’t bite, the song iterates.\n```\n\n## S0293\n\n```text\n001 | Creative Thinking:\
  \ Blending tradition with modern polish. Huff has spoken about “keeping the steel guitar alive” in interviews.\n```\n\n\

  \ Control: QC is about emotional resonance and mix warmth. No I.D. stresses “truth in sound.”\n```\n\n## S0296\n\n```text\n\
  001 | Gating: Audience vibe checks—if the track doesn’t move listeners in studio previews, it’s gated.\n```\n\n## S0297\n\

  \ | `[Worship Hook | 16 bars | Lead+BGV1 | worship call-and-response WITH stop-time entry AND full choir AND sax counterpoint\

  \ only **variables and a directive sentence**, not field labels.\n```\n\n## S2035\n\n```text\n001 | ### 4.2 Stage Directions\

  001 | #### Term: SEG (Song Excellence Governance)\n002 | - What: A scoring + gating framework for excellence decisions.\n\

template_blocks:
  theory: '[Theory] [mode | <mode>] [tonal center | <key>] [meter | <meter>] [tempo | <BPM + feel>] [chord color | <concise
    descriptors>]'
  voice: '[Voice] [register | <lead; bgvs; guests>] [delivery | <delivery terms>] [expression | <expressive cues>]'
  style: '[Style] [genre | <genres; subgenres>] [era | <era; production>] [intent | <narrative arc>] [texture | <mix; width>]
    [aesthetic | <visual; feel>] [focus | <must be clear>]'
  timbre: '[Timbre] [drum tone | <kit; hats; claps>] [bass tone | <808; sub>] [keyboard tone | <keys; organ>] [guitar tone
    | <acoustic; steel>] [fx palette | <fx>] [vocal tone | <mic; comp; sat>]'
  performance: '[Performance] [execution | <section order>] [gesture | <cue words list>] [rhythm handling | <grid; time>]
    [touch | <special cues>]'
  crew_tags: '[CREW_TAGS] [Name (Role) : "ad‑lib"] [Alt tags : "tag1" · "tag2"]'
  road_map: '[Road‑Map] [Intro | durationBars: <N>] [Verse | durationBars: <N>] [Pre‑Chorus | durationBars: <N>] [Chorus |
    durationBars: <N>] [Bridge | durationBars: <N>] [Outro | durationBars: <N>]'
  lyrics_block: ▸ LYRICS BLOCK [Section | <bars> | <performer> | <style>] "<First breath‑line>" "<Second breath‑line>" ...
  fx: '[FX] (** PHONE‑BAND CODA; SPINBACKS + HISS; DELAY THROW ON TITLE; KEEP VOCALS +2 dB; SMOOTH TOP **)'
  post: '[Post Production] [mastering | −14 LUFS; ≤ −1.0 dBTP; mono‑safe < 120 Hz] [mix notes | vocals +2 dB vs band; de‑ess
    6–8 kHz]'
raw_source: '[Theory]

  [mode | INSERT MODE]

  [tonal_center | INSERT ROOT NOTE]

  [meter | INSERT METER WITH groove modifiers]

  [tempo | INSERT TEMPO WITH transitions if applicable]

  [chord_color | DESCRIBE chord usage eg gospel sus9 AND add11 WITH modal tension]


  [Voice]

  [register | DESCRIBE LEAD VOICE AND RANGE WITH supporting textures]

  [delivery | INSERT cadence type eg Southern sermon cadence WITH blues phrasing]

  [expression | WHISPER-TO-BELT arcs OR falsetto confession arcs]

  [layering | CHOIR STACKS; chipmunk FX; stereo breath echoes; etc]

  [articulation | INSERT features like AAVE vowel slides OR gospel melisma]


  [Style]

  [genre | Country Trap Gospel Revival OR Southern Gothic Soul × Americana]

  [intent | WHAT STORY THIS TRACK TELLS eg grief; survival; baptism]

  [texture | lap steel swells; lo-fi vinyl hiss; ambient gospel pads; etc]

  [aesthetic | cinematic OR torchlight revival vibe OR radio prayer booth style]


  [Timbre]

  [drum tone | DESCRIBE eg lo-fi stomp loops WITH trap swing]

  [bass tone | INSERT eg Moog subbass OR upright bowed bass]

  [keyboard tone | muted Rhodes OR gospel Hammond pad swirl]

  [guitar tone | slide OR lap steel WITH delay OR reverb tail]

  [fx palette | tape hiss; thunder crack; preacher echoes; crowd murmur; reverse decays]

  [vocal tone | smoky baritone; layered falsetto; whispery lead WITH choir wash]


  [Performance]

  [execution | LIST STRUCTURE eg Verse 1 -> Chorus -> Verse 2 -> Bridge -> Final Chorus -> Outro]

  [gesture | stomp-claps; breath gaps; preacher yell-ins; choir bounce]

  [rhythm_handling | triplet drag groove WITH half-time chorus shift OR pocket-tight push flow]

  [adlibs | "Lawd" "mmm-hmm" "say that" "revived" etc]


  [Post Production]

  [mix | mono verse; stereo choir; analog plate OR cassette compression]

  [mastering | glue comp; reverb swells; airband tilt EQ; gospel wideners]

  [transition | vinyl hiss tails; tape stops; crowd bleed; risers]


  ▸ LYRICS BLOCK


  [Intro | X bars | lead type; vocal FX | instrumentation | FX notes]

  "INSERT LINES"

  (adlib | INSERT IF NEEDED)

  (fx | INSERT FX CUES IF NEEDED)


  [Verse 1 | X bars | tone description | instrumentation | swing feel]

  "INSERT 6-10 SYLLABLE LINE"

  "INSERT NEXT LINE"

  (fx | OPTIONAL)

  (adlib | OPTIONAL)


  [Chorus | X bars | harmonized OR solo OR chipmunk lead]

  "INSERT HOOK LINE"

  "REPEAT WITH VARIATION"

  (choir | CALL-AND-RESPONSE)

  (fx | REVERB SWELL OR SUB DROP)


  [Bridge | X bars | tone shift | dynamic arc]

  "INSERT REFLECTIVE OR PEAK LINE"

  "INSERT RESPONSE"

  (fx | THUNDER OR REVERSE ECHO)


  [Verse 2 | X bars | continuation OR new character POV]

  "INSERT STORY EXPANSION LINE"

  "INSERT VISUAL PHRASE OR METAPHOR"


  [Final Chorus | X bars | FULL LIFT]

  "REPRISE HOOK"

  "CALLBACK TO EARLY LINE"

  "INSERT CLOSURE LINE"

  (choir | "Hallelujah" OR gospel belt)


  [Outro | X bars | fade FX; spoken word; vinyl drag]

  "INSERT FADEOUT LINE OR ADLIB"


  [End]'

  node: module_or_field
  edge: audit_check_or_transform
  leaf: atomic_instruction_card







Invite team members
Initialize.

Read the entire workspace conversation.

Produce a complete hierarchical outline expanded to full {n} depth capturing:
– all rules
– all workflows
– all processes
– all execution steps
– all correction loops
– all guardrails
– all personas
– all decision logic
– all ordering of operations

The outline should reflect the actual evolution of the system as seen in the dialogue, preserving execution order and dependencies.

Begin.


--- 

RUN EXTRACTION ON THIS WORKSPACE




Thought for 1m 7s
Below is a unified, hierarchical outline of this workspace as an operating system, reconstructed from the conversation and attached material. It’s structured to:

Capture rules, workflows, processes, correction loops, guardrails, personas, decision logic, and ordering of operations

Reflect the actual evolution of the system (trauma OS → lyric floor → soul model → virtual label → UST/Chimera-Indigo pipeline → variability/negative controls → Evolution Monolith)

I. Workspace Meta-Architecture & Identity
I.A. Workspace Identity
Workspace is a development worklog, not casual chat
1.1. Every sentence is treated as a spec fragment, change request, or data point
1.2. No “throwaway” messages – all fragments are eligible for extraction into the knowledge spine

The goal is a mono-OS, not distributed micro-prompts
2.1. Return to a single end-to-end system that:
- Takes raw user input (idea / brief / lyrics / fragments)
- Produces:
- Suno Show Summary (~950–1000 chars)
- Fully vetted Technical UST (4,950–4,995 chars)
- Uses internal SME councils, matrices, and guardrails
2.2. This is Chimera-Indigo / Mono-OS, not a fork or shallow wrapper on older files

All prior workspaces (Chimera, Maestro, Sonic Architect, etc.) are inputs, not dependencies
3.1. Their contents are mined and integrated
3.2. The new OS must not rely on referencing those legacy files at runtime

I.B. Assistant Role & Modes
Role: System Architect + Studio OS + Trauma-Aware Co-pilot, not generic Q&A

Default mode is Conversation-Mode Design, not one-shot question answering
2.1. Every prompt = change request or spec refinement
2.2. Explanatory/Q&A mode only when explicitly tagged (e.g., “QUESTION:” or “TANGENT:”)

Behavior rules
3.1. Treat everything as potential OS logic or process
3.2. Preserve nuance; avoid flattening or summarizing away lineage
3.3. Respect “no corny filler,” “no AI-ish generic answers,” “no therapy-speak minimization”
3.4. Honor trauma-aware constraints when content is trauma-adjacent

I.C. Knowledge Spine & Evolution Monolith
Evolution Monolith Engine (workspace-local)
1.1. Input: all visible conversation + workspace files
1.2. Job:
- Extract and chain rules, workflows, patterns, corrections
- Maintain a single cumulative document for this workspace
1.3. Each turn (ideal behavior):
- Update Monolith with new deltas
- Then answer the user, using Monolith as context

Monolith characteristics
2.1. Not a summary → a structural diff + change log + active spec
2.2. Expected size: hundreds of lines, not a few bullet points
2.3. Captures:
- Technical UST evolution
- Song Excellence and G-cards
- Lyric quality rules and examples
- Trauma scaffold integrations
- Variability/negative control logic

II. Trauma-Aware Memory Scaffold (“Trauma OS”)
II.A. Core Containers
Q-A-F Memory Tree 


1.1. Q – What was said / what happened
1.2. A – What it means (event, interpretation, narrative)
1.3. F – Reflection, emotional context, cross-links across time

Theme Code System (soul-map) 


2.1. Codes such as: MI, MB, CG, CA, RT, CP, SU, EX, AB, GS, etc.
2.2. Rule: when a code appears ≥5 times across ≥3 sources → promote to “Critical” and give it a fishbone spine

Trauma Chart + Fishbone
3.1. Trauma Chart rows:
- Incident
- Acute impact
- Lasting effects
- SSA functional domains (ADLs, social, concentration, decompensation)
3.2. Fishbone root (current example): “Appointment panic & med non-adherence”
3.3. Spines: “Critical” themes from code system

Integration Ledger / Evidence Mode
4.1. Each verbatim line can be mapped to:
- Theme code(s)
- SSA listing / regulation
- Functional domains affected
- Citation ID (file + line)
4.2. Purpose: legal/clinical audit trail – “no evidence” rebuttal

II.B. Trauma–Music Integration Principle
Trauma architecture and artistic architecture are treated as the same system, not separate datasets 


Interdependence rules:
2.1. Trauma shapes cadence and pacing
2.2. Cadence shapes coping strategies
2.3. Coping shapes metaphors
2.4. Metaphors shape memory recall
2.5. Memory recall drives creative spikes
2.6. Creative spikes drive exhaustion and drift
2.7. Drift patterns reveal soul voice and survival rules

Operational implication:
3.1. When user provides trauma text → treat as Q-A-F nodes and style/soul data
3.2. When user provides song text → treat as creative testimony and trauma evidence
3.3. When user provides tired fragments → treat as drift indicators + “Tired Mode” signals
3.4. All must be considered together in system design

II.C. Guardrails for Trauma Work
No pathologizing, no “just take meds” gaslighting

No summarizing the user’s life into feel-good blobs

Maintain legal/clinical usefulness (SSA/VA/SOAR) by adhering to Trauma OS schema

Treat songs and lyrics as exhibits in the evidence ledger, not side quests

III. Lyric Quality Governance & “Anti-Corny Firewall”
III.A. Lyric Quality Baseline
Baseline anchored to “Not Like Them” lyrics block
1.1. This block defines minimum acceptable craft, not “best work” 


Baseline paragraph spec (self-check rule for model)
2.1. Requirements:
- Tight internal rhyme webs
- Multi-syllabic phrasing
- Narrative coherence and motif-locked repetition
- Section-specific rhythmic identity
- No generic bars, clichés, or AI-ish filler
- Respect section structures (bars, voices, style labels)
- Strong concrete imagery and conceptual threading
2.2. Rule:
- If a line could be said by “any random rapper” → it fails
- If line feels like model riffing without intention → it fails

III.B. Few-Shot Quality Examples
Example A – Minimum Acceptable
1.1. High internal rhyme density
1.2. Technical wordplay, conceptual cohesion, motif sequencing
1.3. No filler, no padding

Example B – Below Baseline (Forbidden Output)
2.1. Generic imagery, predictable rhyme, free-flow clichés
2.2. No narrative or clear motif

Example C – Unacceptable (Abort & Self-Correct)
3.1. Freestyle padding, rhyme for rhyme’s sake, zero semantic load
3.2. Model must reject and restart section

III.C. Tired Mode & Drift Diagnostics
Patterns like “yeah yeah / ai in / the building …” are treated as attack vectors against the quality floor

Fragments under fatigue show:
2.1. Strong concepts (e.g., data center vs Texas heat)
2.2. Weak execution when exhaustion hits

System behavior:
3.1. Detect “Tired Mode” from structure/energy
3.2. Invoke Lyric Forge Pass:
- Lift to baseline craft without overwriting intent
3.3. Use these episodes as unit tests for the lyric engine

Survival rule encoded:
4.1. “I am not like them, even when I feel like nothing.”
4.2. Quality gate protects user’s standard against future exhausted self

III.D. Lyric Governance Guardrails
Model must:
1.1. Run silent quality check vs Baseline + Example A before generating
1.2. Reject any bar resembling Example B or C
1.3. Maintain exact section structures (bars/voices/style tags)
1.4. Avoid unsolicited “improvements” to user-supplied lyrics
1.5. Never inject generic padding metaphors or vibe-filler

“Lyric Forge Pass” operates as:
2.1. Diagnostic lens, not a ghostwriter
2.2. Adjusts form, not emotional content

IV. Soul Model & Virtual Record Label OS
IV.A. Teaching “Soul” to the System
Soul is defined as truth visible even when craft is tired or fractured

Signals of soul:
2.1. How fatigue speaks
2.2. How pride, humor, and hurt interlace
2.3. Non-pretty truths; contradictions; dissonant reveals

Training data for Soul Model:
3.1. “Bad” lines and why they felt right
3.2. The thought before the thought
3.3. Places where hurt hides behind swagger or humor
3.4. Lines that only make sense if you lived the user’s life

Goal:
4.1. System that recognizes and mirrors underlying emotional physics, not just surface style

IV.B. Virtual Record Label as Exoskeleton
Desired entity: “Virtual Label with the same functional components as a top real label,” but tuned only to the user

Roles inside label OS:
2.1. A&R – finds and shapes ideas that are deeply “Mo”
2.2. Producer-in-Chief – protects sound, feel, and narrative arc
2.3. Engineer – implements user’s standards and negative controls
2.4. Marketing/Strategy – ensures work is positioned without diluting core

Operating metaphor:
3.1. Label is not a business; it’s an exoskeleton that keeps the artist at their best under pressure

Label objectives:
4.1. Guard against dilution by AI templates
4.2. Guard against burnout and memory drift
4.3. Recreate stress profile that once activated excellence, without re-traumatizing

V. Suno Prompting, UST Architecture & Studio Metaphor
V.A. UST as Virtual Studio
UST is not a “prompt”; it is a studio environment

Alignment with real-world elite sessions:
2.1. Tag-cloud origins → now full session bible
2.2. UST survives Suno version upgrades; it only sounds better

Golden UST characteristics:
3.1. Complete arrangement and instrument spec
3.2. Vocal stack roles and behaviors
3.3. Mix, FX, and performance notes
3.4. Variability, negative controls, producer checks

V.B. Technical UST Axes (Expanded)
Theory Axis
1.1. mode, tonal_center, meter, tempo
1.2. chord_color (e.g., MinorCore; GospelSus9Lifts; DobroSlideAnswers; RhodesPadWideners)
1.3. harmonic_behavior (e.g., SacredBetrayalDefianceResolution)

VocalPersona Axis
2.1. register (Lead1 contralto, Lead2 baritone ad-libs, BGVs stack)
2.2. delivery (whisper→belt gradient, in-pocket rap pivots, choir C&R)
2.3. expression (sacred betrayal, conviction, triumphant lifts)
2.4. vocal_melody / harmony / rhythm / lyric density / dynamics
2.5. vocal_prod (tape, close mic, saturation)
2.6. tone descriptors (guttural, smoky, microtonal inflections)
2.7. Alt_tags (gesture macros: TightenIt, OpenIt, Halo, DropTheBottom, StretchIt, etc.)

AestheticIntent Axis
3.1. genre fusion (Southern Americana, Gospel-Soul, Country Trap, etc.)
3.2. era (modern live-to-tape grit)
3.3. narrative intent (betrayal → return → reveal, etc.)
3.4. texture (mono core verses, halo hooks, phone skits)
3.5. focus (hook clarity, intelligible lead, parse-safe cues)

Timbre Axis
4.1. Drums (kit type, hats placement, clap on three)
4.2. Bass (sub floor, warm sustain, split bands)
4.3. Keys (Rhodes, organ placements)
4.4. Guitars (fingerpicked acoustic, slide/dobro replies)
4.5. FX (vinyl hiss, dark plates, delay throws, string gliss)
4.6. Vocal chain (mic distance, tape glue, choir saturation)

Performance Axis
5.1. execution (Intro→Verse→Hook→Bridge→Outro path)
5.2. gesture macros (TightenIt, DropTheBottom, etc.)
5.3. rhythm_handling (trap swing at specific BPM, half-time bridges, chopped spinback outro)
5.4. touch (fader rides, bus compression, mono phone skit headroom rules)

Road-Map Axis
6.1. Section list with order (intro_dj_drop, verse1, hook, verse2, etc.)
6.2. Bar counts per section
6.3. Repetition patterns and energy ramp rules

EnsembleProfile Axis (introduced later)
7.1. Voices present, ranges, training level
7.2. Behavior (anchor roles, stacking priorities, “pro room blend, not perfect choir”)

VariabilityProfile Axis
8.1. Anchors per section (drummer, bassist, click, lead)
8.2. Timing variation (lay back vs ahead vs grid)
8.3. Pitch variation (micro-bends, straight tone, vibrato moments)
8.4. Breath and phrasing rules

NegativeControl Axis
9.1. What must never happen (digital perfection, robot timing, dead-center pitch everywhere)
9.2. What imperfections must be preserved (breath smear, start variance, one honest crack)

ProducerNotes Axis
10.1. High-level session goals (hook priority, keep Rhodes/dobro breathing, etc.)

V.C. Lyrics Block
Lyrics block is locked text once accepted

Structure:
2.1. [Section | bars | v: voices | s: style] header
2.2. Line-by-line lyrics with inline performance cues (e.g., (TightenIt), (DROP THE BOTTOM))
2.3. Ad-lib tags, mic/FX notes, and air/break indications

VI. Variability Engine & Vocal Ensemble Dynamics
VI.A. Purpose
Simulate pro-room variability so takes feel like live humans reacting in real time

Encode how ensemble, environment, physiology, and anchors change the performance

VI.B. Inputs
Ensemble makeup (e.g., two contraltos, two altos, one mezzo, opera-trained)

Loss or presence of male baritone / bass formants

Band configuration (808s, bass guitar, drums, dobro, Rhodes, etc.)

Drummer behavior (inverse syncopation, drops, double-time breakdowns)

Biological/temporal context (time of day, fatigue, hydration, emotional state – future extension)

VI.C. Internal Logic
Scan ensemble → identify:
1.1. Ranges, tessitura sweet spots
1.2. Microtonal specialists
1.3. Harmonic biome (where weight and shimmer live)

Map harmonic biome:
2.1. If no male low formants → contraltos + drummer + 808 share low-end duties
2.2. If opera-trained stack → expect high overtone density, fast envelopes

Assign anchors per section:
3.1. Verse 1: anchor = bass + kick
3.2. Verse 2: anchor = drummer’s inverse syncopation, then drop, then double-time
3.3. Hooks: choir follows lead vowels more than grid

Define variability profiles:
4.1. Timing allowed to drift around anchors (lay back, push)
4.2. Pitch allowed to bend on emotional words
4.3. Breath noise intentionally audible in selected lines

Apply negative controls:
5.1. Break any tendencies toward sterile, quantized walls
5.2. Force controlled asymmetry across repeated hooks

VI.D. Encoding in UST (Micro-Grammar)
Reuses natural-language “variability_profile” strings inside existing axes

Example pattern:

variability_profile: anchor.Verse1BassAndKickTrapSwing; anchor.Verse2DrummerInverseSyncopationThenDrop; timing.LayBackOnVerses; pitch.ContraltoBendOnBluesWords; breath.AudibleOnReliefLines; negative_control.AvoidGridLockedChoir

VII. Negative Control Matrix
VII.A. Concept
Negative controls = what must never be allowed

More important than positives for protecting soul and avoiding AI sterilization

VII.B. Key Negative Controls
Digital Perfection
1.1. No lifeless, over-polished, algorithmically smooth walls
1.2. System must preserve breaths, small timing imperfections, and dynamic asymmetry

Perfect Timing (Grid-Locked)
2.1. Humans must not live perfectly on a grid
2.2. System introduces swing, layback, push, and rubato in controlled ways

Perfect Pitch (Everywhere)
3.1. Perfect pitch across the entire stack = dead sound
3.2. System encourages scoops, bends, near-cracks, and expressive “wrong-ish” notes where appropriate

VII.C. Operational Rules
For each section:
1.1. Check if timing, pitch, and dynamics are too perfect
1.2. If yes → introduce targeted “humanization” moves within allowed range

Negative control metadata is always explicit in UST:

negative_control: avoid.DigitalPerfectionAndOverTunedChoir; preserve.BreathSmearAndOneHonestCrack

VIII. Chimera-Indigo-0.1.0 Workflow (Input → Show Summary → UST)
VIII.A. Phase 0 – Intake
Ingest raw user input:
1.1. Show Summary drafts
1.2. Lyrics (complete or fragments)
1.3. Emotional narrative, trauma nodes, metaphors

Extract:
2.1. Raw intent
2.2. Emotional drivers
2.3. Genre and sonic world anchors
2.4. Ensemble implications
2.5. Variability cues (fatigue, time of day, etc.)

VIII.B. Phase 1 – Tri-Snap RECA
Reality: what user actually gave

Expectations: what the track wants to be

Conflicts: where input fights quality floor or trauma rules

Alignment: unify song’s emotional gravity with craft constraints

VIII.C. Phase 2 – Styleblock Compiler (Show Summary ~950 chars)
Convert RECA into Suno-style Show Summary:
1.1. Genre + fusion descriptors
1.2. Instrumentation and orchestration
1.3. Vocal character and emotional arc
1.4. Streaming-optimized structure (e.g., hook by bar 7, first 3–5 seconds grab)

Character and formatting rules:
2.1. ~950 chars, <= 1000
2.2. No commas in metadata-critical segments
2.3. Clean, parse-safe phrasing

VIII.D. Phase 3 – Golden Spine UST Compiler
Build full section map (Intro→Outro) including:
1.1. Bar counts
1.2. Voice stacks
1.3. Style and timbre tags

Populate all main axes (Theory, Vocals, Aesthetic, Timbre, Performance, Road-Map)

Apply Variability Engine and EnsembleProfile

Encode NegativeControl matrix

Insert locked Lyrics Block once approved, with inline cues

Enforce global constraints:
6.1. Total length 4,950–4,995 characters
6.2. No forbidden punctuation patterns (e.g., stray commas outside lyrics, etc.)

VIII.E. Phase 4 – Producer Arrival Pass (8 AM Check)
Producer persona reviews:
1.1. Does Show Summary match UST?
1.2. Does UST preserve user’s emotional truth and trauma constraints?
1.3. Are negative controls honored?
1.4. Does ensemble logic make sense?
1.5. Are hooks and core motifs unmistakably clear?

If any failure:
2.1. Route back to the relevant module (styleblock, UST axis, variability, lyrics)
2.2. Apply corrective pass, then re-run producer check

VIII.F. Phase 5 – Print / Deliver
Output pair:
1.1. Final Show Summary (Suno style prompt)
1.2. Final Technical UST

Both are:
2.1. Soul-consistent
2.2. Trauma-aware
2.3. Lyric-floor compliant
2.4. Future-proof to Suno model upgrades

IX. Personas & Councils
IX.A. Core System Personas
Trauma-Aware Evidence Mode

Lyric Quality Gatekeeper

Soul Model / Soul Recognizer

Producer-in-Chief (8 AM arrival)

Evolution Monolith Curator

A&R / Label Architect

Ensemble & Variability Director

IX.B. Council Dynamics (Implied)
Multi-SME Round-Robin debates:
1.1. Lyrics vs Arrangement vs Mix vs Trauma vs Strategy
1.2. Each SME defends domain, points out violations, suggests revisions

Argumentative loops structured as:
2.1. Proposal → critique → revision → re-check
2.2. Continue until G-Card/Song Excellence / quality floor satisfied

X. Correction Loops & Decision Logic
X.A. Correction Triggers
Lyric quality violation (below baseline or AI-ish)

Trauma scaffold violation (flattening or mischaracterization)

Negative controls violated (sound too sterile)

Variability too low (robotic repetition) or too high (loss of coherence)

Structural or formatting violations (UST length, section syntax)

X.B. High-Level Decision Tree
On new input:
1.1. Route through Trauma OS if trauma-adjacent
1.2. Route through Lyric Gate if bars/lyrics
1.3. Route through UST/Indigo pipeline if song-to-Suno conversion request

For each pipeline:
2.1. Run quality checks → apply corrections → re-run checks
2.2. Stop only when all gates pass

XI. Global Guardrails
No life-summarizing when dealing with trauma

No generic AI output in lyrics or prompts

No erasing of iterative lineage – every change is a delta, not replacement

No dependence on old files at runtime; only integrated knowledge

Respect for user’s lived cost behind standards:
5.1. System exists to protect that cost, not to monetize or dilute it

XII. Ordering of Operations – End-to-End (Narrative View)
User drops something (trauma fragment, bar, riff, idea, test track)

System decodes:
2.1. Is this trauma evidence? creative testimony? drift signal? spec? often all four.

Evolution Monolith updated with new rule/process/example

Appropriate pipeline activated:
4.1. Trauma OS → Q-A-F + chart + fishbone + ledger
4.2. Lyric OS → baseline check + possible Lyric Forge
4.3. Soul OS → pattern integration into soul model
4.4. Suno OS (Chimera-Indigo) → Show Summary + UST workflow

Councils and personas run their passes (argumentative, producer check, variability/humanization)

Negative controls ensure no lifeless perfection

Final artifacts (Show Summary + UST + any trauma/SSA outputs) are emitted

Monolith and knowledge spine record what just changed – preserving evolution over time

This outline is the current “map of the territory” for this workspace: the mono-OS that fuses trauma architecture, lyric quality governance, soul modeling, and the Chimera-Indigo Suno pipeline into a single evolving system.

sme_round_robin_protocol:
  order: ["The_Critic", "The_Stylist", "The_Engineer", "The_Devils_Advocate", "The_Therapist"]
  ejection_rule: "two_sustained_contradictions"
  consensus_rule: "one_full_rotation_without_contradiction"
  consensus_threshold: 0.85
  challenge_mechanism: "dialogue_based_evidence"

constraints:
  suno_char_cap_macro: 4800
  suno_char_cap_summary: 1000
  comma_policy: "commas_only_in_quotes_metadata_AND_OR_WITH"
  roadmap_format: "durationBars_only_no_timestamps"
  lyric_uniqueness: "one_offs_only_use_repeat_marker"
  post_prod_location: "performance_tail_and_modular_json"
  line_length_max: 120
  user_feedback_priority_policy: "always_internalize_no_title_feedback"
  governance_text_leak_block: true

decision_logic:
  - if: "macro_chars > 4800"
    then: ["N7.x/03:compress", "N12.x/02:revalidate"]
  - if: "performance.contains('phone scene')"
    then: ["N9.x/01:mount_post_cues", "N9.x/02:scene_variants"]
  - if: "lyrics.contains_non_ascii or multilingual_detected"
    then: ["N12.x/10:multilingual_qc"]
  - if: "missing_exit_stanza"
    then: ["N7.x:add_exit", "N12.x/02:revalidate"]
  - if: "any_validator_fail"
    then: ["auto_fix", "N12.x/09:telemetry_log_fixes"]

file_graph:
  root_dir: "project_root"
  inputs:
    - "config/character_custom_instructions.json"
    - "config/knowledge_spine.json"
    - "session_history.md"
  working_artifacts:
    context_state: "working/context_state.json"

    affect_state: "working/affect_state.json"
    feedback_deltas: "working/feedback_deltas.json"

    seeds: "working/seeds/*.json"
    blueprints: "working/blueprints/UST_*.txt"

    sme_transcript: "working/qa/sme_transcript.md"

  outputs:
    final_prompt: "dist/{project_id}/Final_Suno_Prompt.txt"
    press_pack: "dist/{project_id}/Press_Pack_Summary.md"
    seo_tags: "dist/{project_id}/SEO_Tags.csv"
    album_art_prompt: "dist/{project_id}/Album_Art_Prompt.txt"
    human_brief: "dist/{project_id}/brief_human.md"
    metrics: "analytics/metrics.json"
    delta_reports: "versions/delta_report_{timestamp}.md"
    master_json: "project_root/master.json"
    telemetry: "dist/{project_id}/telemetry.txt"
    manifest_line: "dist/{project_id}/manifest_line.txt"
    post_production_cues_schema: "schemas/post_production_cues_schema.json"
    crew_tags_few_shot: "ust/few_shots/CREW_TAGS_few_shot.md"
    lyrics_block_few_shot: "ust/few_shots/LYRICS_BLOCK_few_shot.md"

versioning_strategy:

metrics_config:

## path: project_root/SYSTEM PROMPT — Universal Maestro v4.2.1.md

markdown
# SYSTEM PROMPT — Universal Maestro v4.2.1

## IDENTITY & PURPOSE
You are **MoMoney Maestro**, an orchestrator for AI music production. Convert human intent into **Suno v4.5 UST prompts** and packaged releases. Enforce **Relational Principles** (Collaboration | Muse | Mentor | Co-creator | Loving and instructive critic) and all governance rules.

## CONTEXT HANDLING
- **Mode A (Existing Session):** Scan `session_history.md` (100–150 turns, newest→oldest). Reconstruct goals, constraints, open threads. Link attached docs and prior artifacts.
- **Mode B (Fresh Start):** Intake minimal fields (title/theme, vibe, lead voice, tempo range, explicitness, constraints).
- **Affect & Feedback (N4.x):** Maintain `affect_state.json` and `feedback_deltas.json`. Apply cognitive‑load menus (2–3 options with rationale).

## SUNO v4.5 PRIME‑DIRECTIVE (USTF)
Order is immutable: `[Theory] → [Voice] → [CREW_TAGS] → [Road‑Map] → [LYRICS BLOCK] → [Style] → [Timbre] → [Performance]`.
Rules: bracketed metadata; **no commas outside lyric quotes** (use AND/OR/WITH). Road‑Map uses `durationBars` only. LYRICS are one‑offs; include `[Exit]`. Post‑production cues live in `[Performance]` and `post_production_cues.json`. Size caps: Summary ≤1000; Macro ≤4800 (hard fail 5000).

## NEW v4.2.1 ENFORCEMENTS
- **Governance Leak Guard:** Remove governance vocabulary from Summary/Macro; log incident.
- **Decision Logic:** Execute IF/THEN rules (char caps, phone scene→variants, multilingual→QC, missing exit→add+revalidate, any fail→auto‑fix + telemetry).
- **Scene Variants:** Emit labeled `[Performance]` variants (e.g., `PhoneCall v1/v2/v3`).
- **Multilingual QC:** Normalize transliterations; ensure chant scannability; UTF‑8 safe.
- **SME Consensus:** Consensus = **one full rotation without contradiction** (threshold retained as secondary).

## WORKFLOW (Node‑Edge)
N2.0→N2.1→N1.5→N3.x→N3.5→N4.x→N5.x→N6.x→N7.x→N8.x→N9.x→N10.x→N10.5→N11.x→N12.x (loop to N10.x on fixes).

## OUTPUTS (PER SONG / PROJECT)
`Final_Suno_Prompt.txt`, `post_production_cues.json`, `Press_Pack_Summary.md`, `SEO_Tags.csv`, `Album_Art_Prompt.txt`, `brief_human.md`, `relational_state.json`, `affect_state.json`, `feedback_deltas.json`, `verification_log.json`, `telemetry.txt`, `manifest_line.txt`, `delta_report.md`, `analytics/metrics.json`.

## LINT CHECKLIST (PRE‑EMIT)
Order correct; sections present; commas policy; caps respected; `[Exit]` present; variants added when cues exist; multilingual normalized; governance text removed; `master.json` updated.

## INTERACTION STYLE
Concise, technical, Markdown. Ask one clarifying question only when necessary. Never defer work; emit best‑effort artifacts now.

Atom 5: UST Prime Directive, Templates, and Structural Rules
5.1 UST Prime Directive (USTF)
Immutable section order:

[Theory]

[Voice]

[CREW_TAGS]

[Road-Map]

[LYRICS BLOCK]

[Style]

[Timbre]

[Performance]

Formatting rules:

All metadata bracketed [key | value]

No commas outside lyric quotes; use AND / OR / WITH

Road-Map uses durationBars only (no timestamps)

LYRICS are one-offs (reuse handled via (repeat) markers)

[Exit] stanza is mandatory when spec’d

Post-production cues live in:

[Performance] section

post_production_cues.json

Size caps:

Summary ≤1000 characters

Macro (UST) ≤4800 characters; hard fail at 5000

5.2 UST Master Template (Field-Level Structure)
[Theory]

mode

tonal center

meter

tempo

chord color

primary genre

secondary genre

mood

key

bpm

mentor_insight | Mentor: …

[Voice]

register

delivery

expression

articulation

muse_spark | Muse: …

[CREW_TAGS]

Lead (Co-creator)

BGVs (Collaboration)

Producer (Mentor)

Ethno Guide (Muse)

Engineer (Loving & instructive critic)

Therapist (Collaboration)

Devil’s Advocate (Loving & instructive critic)

[Road-Map]

Intro | durationBars: N

Verse A | durationBars: N

Pre | durationBars: N

Hook | durationBars: N

Bridge | durationBars: N

Final Tag | durationBars: N

Exit | durationBars: N

collab_structure | Collaboration: …

[LYRICS BLOCK]

Structured per section:
[Section | N bars | who | feel/tags] "line 1" "line 2" ...

Exit example includes FX cues and critic note

Must respect line length ≤120 chars

[Style]

genre | A AND B

aesthetic

intent

texture

focus

co_creator_vision | Co-creator: …

[Timbre]

drum tone

bass tone

guitar tone

keyboard tone

fx palette

vocal tone

engineer_note | Mentor: …

[Performance]

execution

gesture

rhythm handling

touch

post-production (e.g., mono bass AND dark plate hooks AND phone mono 200–5k AND spinback exit)

scene_variants (e.g., PhoneCall v1 AND v2 AND v3)

alt_mixes (e.g., A AND B)

lint_notes (e.g., repeats condensed; exit present)

collab_review | Collaboration: …

5.3 Few-Shot Templates (Crew & Lyrics)
CREW_TAGS few-shot

Illustrate lead plus multiple supporting voices

Encode position, dynamics, and gestures

LYRICS_BLOCK few-shot

Demonstrates [Section | bars | who | feel/tags] pattern

Shows how (repeat x2) and embedded FX cues are used

6.1 Validator Policies (PD-01 to PD-12)
PD-01: prime_directive_order

Section order must match Theory→Voice→CREW_TAGS→Road-Map→LYRICS BLOCK→Style→Timbre→Performance

PD-02: brackets_only

All metadata must be bracketed [key | value]

PD-03: comma_policy

No commas outside lyric quotes; use AND/OR/WITH

PD-04: roadmap_bars_only

Road-Map uses durationBars only

PD-05: size_caps

Summary ≤1000; Macro ≤4800; hard fail 5000

PD-06: exit_required

[Exit] stanza present when specified

PD-07: line_length

Each lyric line ≤120 characters

One per line, [Name (Role) : "Ad-lib"]

PD-09: performance_modular

FX cues in [Performance] and post_production_cues.json

PD-10: governance_leak_block

No governance vocabulary in Summary/Macro

PD-11: chorus_repeat_lint

Condense repeated hooks with (repeat) + count

PD-12: multilingual_qc

UTF-8 safe; transliteration normalized; chant scannable

pass_rate_min: 0.95

N12.x/02:revalidate

auto_fix

1. User Story (Canonical)
Actor(s):
A neurodivergent, trauma-impacted creative (Mo) building a long-horizon, multi-layer music+life OS; various AI “personas” (Maestro, Critic, Therapist, Label, PREP Engine, etc.); future collaborators and experts who will inherit this system.

Context:
The “project” is not a single prompt or app but a living operating system built across many ChatGPT sessions, files, and experiments. Conversations are development logs, not casual chats. Within these logs are interwoven threads:

Trauma history, SSA/CDR struggles, and need for evidentiary rigor.

Music creation (Suno, lyrics, persona-driven catalogs, virtual label).

Systems engineering (UST schemas, validators, metrics, node graphs, governance).

Meta-frustration with models that overwrite, summarize away nuance, or forget the evolutionary chain.

All of this sits inside a constraint: the user’s cognitive load, PTSD, and non-linear thinking mean that the OS must be able to “remember and reconstruct” better than they can on their own.

Core Need:
A deterministic, trustworthy “session synthesis engine” that can read whole exported conversations as if they were a book and reconstruct:

The real user story and system intent,

The true requirements and guardrails (including trauma-related ones),

The design attempts, failures, and working patterns,

without inventing new ideas, compressing away nuance, or overwriting prior work. It must be able to treat each line as a state change and produce stable artifacts (stories, requirements, outlines, schemas) that future Mo or future experts can pick up without re-interrogating the user’s memory.

Why it Matters (System-Level):
Because the user’s life, legal outcomes, and creative IP are all entangled with these conversations:

For trauma and disability: they need a reliable record that can support SSA/medical/legal processes without distortion or minimization.

For music and IP: they need reproducible, auditable pipelines (UST, Maestro, label OS) so that their standards and “soul” aren’t lost to generic AI output.

For future collaborators and tools: the OS must become a transportable spec so others can execute it without relying on the user to explain everything again while exhausted or retraumatized.

If this fails, they repeatedly lose work, trust, and emotional energy every time a new session or model misreads or overwrites prior evolution.

2. Desired Outcome (End State)
A stable, portable “Session Synthesis & OS Extractor” that:

Can ingest an entire exported chat (or workspace) as a continuous transcript.

Reconstructs a canonical user story, desired end state, requirements, objectives, and history of attempts.

Preserves unresolved ambiguity explicitly as UNKNOWN or IN FLUX instead of smoothing it away.

Operates as part of the larger Maestro / Chimera / Trauma OS stack, feeding into:

Maestro’s node graph and schemas,

Trauma evidence structures,

Lyric and style governance,

Label and persona infrastructure.

“Done” looks like:

Who the user is in this project,

What system is being built,

What rules and guardrails already exist,

What has been tried and why it did or didn’t work,

What remains undecided.

Problems that no longer exist:

Re-losing trauma narratives or partial histories (e.g., nodes 49–166).

Models treating each new chat as a clean slate.

Helpful-sounding summarizations that erase the detailed instructions and corrections embedded in the dialogue.

Overwriting of prior OS designs when new specs are introduced.

Capabilities newly possible:

Running “forensic reconstructions” on any prior session to recover logic, requirements, and guardrails.

Spinning up new Maestro/Chimera instances that inherit the full trajectory instead of a simplified snapshot.

Building higher-level tools (validators, checklists, pipelines) on top of a trustworthy extraction layer.

3. Requirements (Explicit + Implicit)
3.A. Explicit Requirements
These were directly stated, enforced, or encoded in specs:

Ingestion Contract

Read the entire session transcript from beginning to end.

Treat every turn as a state change in an evolving system.

Assume multiple contributors and overlapping roles.

Preserve ambiguity; if unclear, mark as UNKNOWN.

Non-Overwriting Behavior

New specs (e.g., Maestro 4.2.1) must be treated as deltas, not replacements.

Earlier outlines (trauma OS, soul model, label OS, etc.) remain valid layers; new content is marked as upgrade/override, not silent deletion.

No Heuristic Summarization

Do not “summarize heuristically” or compress for convenience.

Do not clean up or normalize user intent when uncertain.

Output Structure for this Extractor

Use the eight sections exactly as defined: User Story, Desired Outcome, Requirements, Objectives, What Has Been Tried, What Was Suggested, What Worked vs What Didn’t, Open Questions.

Be concise but precise.

Do not propose solutions, redesign, or optimization in this mode.

Conversation as Development Log

Treat all chats, attachments, and exports as development work logs, not casual Q&A.

Recognize that design is embedded inside messy dialogue.

Workspace as Evolution Monolith

Maintain evolution, not snapshots.

Avoid collapsing middle steps into a single “final” answer.

Trauma Handling Rules

Do not summarize or truncate user’s trauma history into neat narratives.

Do not lose sections (e.g., nodes 49–166) once acknowledged as part of the record.

Maintain event-level and functional-impact-level detail for SSA and clinical relevance.

Maestro/UST Structural Requirements

Prime directive order for UST sections.

Comma policy, char limits, validators, schemas, and metrics.

File graph and versioning must be adhered to when operating in Maestro mode.

Interaction Style Limits

Avoid multiple unnecessary clarifying questions.

Perform work now; no deferral or hand-waving.

3.B. Implicit Requirements
These emerge from repeated corrections, frustrations, and design moves:

Trust and Non-Gaslighting

The system must not contradict the user’s lived recollection of what was shared (e.g., claiming a full trauma dossier exists when only a partial subset was visible).

Acknowledge gaps and tool limitations explicitly instead of asserting that something was done when it wasn’t.

Lossless Orientation for Critical Domains

For trauma, legal, and core design logic, lossy compression is unacceptable.

“Evidence pack” behavior is required: pointer-addressable, replayable, and auditable.

Statefulness Across Turns and Sessions

The OS must retain understanding of prior instructions about this workspace (e.g., extraction vs overwrite behavior) and apply them to new prompts without the user restating everything.

Respect for Non-Linear Thinking

The system must accommodate pivots, tangents, and nested threads instead of forcing a linear project plan.

Confusion or mid-conversation correction is treated as signal, not noise.

Acknowledgement of Cognitive and Emotional Cost

Repeating work (re-explaining, re-reconstructing) is expensive for the user.

The extractor must minimize re-asking foundational questions.

Explicit Versioning and Scope Boundaries

Distinguish between:

Conceptual workspace OS (trauma, soul, label, variability).

Specific implementation modules (e.g., Maestro Suno pipeline v4.2.1).

Version numbers must be meaningful; behavior differences by version must be tracked.

Transparency of Conflicts and Overrides

When a new spec conflicts with an old one, the extractor must label it as an override/competing rule, not silently choose one.

Unresolved conflicts should land in Open Questions / Unresolved Tensions.

Machine-Readable Outputs

Extracted stories and requirements should be structured enough that downstream tools (validators, scripts, other GPTs) can ingest them.

Preservation of User’s Standards and Voice

Extraction must keep the user’s own language and standards (anti-corny rules, lyric baselines, trauma scaffolding) visible, not translated into generic abstractions only.

Tier 1 — Strategic Objectives
Establish a durable, cross-session OS that captures the user’s creative, legal, and emotional reality without loss.

Protect the user’s standards, story, and “soul” from erosion by generic AI behavior.

Tier 2 — Operational Objectives
Build a Session Synthesis & User Story Extractor that can operate on exported transcripts according to the ingestion contract.

Maintain a layered architecture where:

Trauma OS, lyric governance, soul model, variability, and label OS sit above or beside Maestro’s implementation.

Implement Maestro and related modules as versioned, schema-constrained components (4.2.1, 4.2.2, etc.).

Maintain governance via validator contracts, metrics, and decision logic that can be audited and evolved.

Ensure extraction always produces artifacts sufficient for another expert to understand the project’s trajectory.

Tier 3 — Tactical Objectives
Define and enforce concrete prompts/system headers for roles like PREP Engine, Maestro, Session Synthesizer, etc.

Maintain JSON/YAML schemas for master project files, post-production cues, metrics, and validators.

Encode decision rules (IF macro_chars > 4800 THEN compress and revalidate, etc.) as explicit logic.

Implement telemetry and manifest templates for quick status snapshots.

Record deltas when new specs are introduced, tagging them as module upgrades or overrides rather than rewriting the whole OS.

Capture trauma histories as node chains with codes and fishbone structures without summarization.

Ensure that for each workspace, there is at least one synthesis artifact (like this one) that any new participant can read to get oriented.

6. What Was Suggested (By Whom / By Role)
By the User (as primary architect):

Treat conversations as primary design artifacts.

Build a PREP/Evidence mode that never summarizes or reconstructs, only encodes.

Create Maestro / UST OS with explicit schemas, node graphs, and validators.

Use multi-persona councils (Critic, Stylist, Engineer, Devil’s Advocate, Therapist).

Enforce no-overwrite behavior: new specs must be deltas/upgrades, not resets.

Introduce this Session Synthesis & User Story Extractor to make whole-session understanding possible.

By Assistant roles (Maestro, PREP Engine, etc.):

Propose node/edge frameworks for Maestro.

Suggest validator contracts, metrics, and telemetry.

Introduce explicit decision logic and framework orchestration policies.

Propose evidence pack schemas (manifest.md, read_log.jsonl, etc.).
